materials.title: A call to the camera shop
materials.text:
Man: Hill Road Camera Shop. How can I help?
Zoe: Hello. I left a small bag in your shop yesterday. Have you found one?
Man: We have two bags here. What colour is yours?
Zoe: It is grey, with a yellow star on the front.
Man: Yes, I can see it. What is inside?
Zoe: A notebook and a pair of red gloves. There is no camera in it.
Man: That matches this one. Please bring something with your name when you collect it.
Zoe: Can I come at six this evening?
Man: We close at five thirty today. We open again at nine tomorrow.
Zoe: I have school tomorrow morning. Could Mum collect it for me?
Man: Yes. Please give her your name and the description of the bag.
Zoe: She can come at four today. Thank you for keeping it safe.
Man: You’re welcome. We will keep it behind the counter.

questions.prompt: What is on Zoe’s bag?
questions.explanation: The bag has a yellow star; red describes gloves and no flower is mentioned.

questions.prompt: What is inside the bag?
questions.explanation: Zoe lists notebook and gloves, explicitly no camera.

questions.prompt: Why can Zoe not collect it at six today?
options: The shop is closed all day
The bag is at her school
questions.explanation: Closing is17:30. The shop is open earlier and holds the bag.

questions.prompt: Who is expected to collect the bag?
questions.explanation: Zoe arranges for Mum to collect it at16:00.

questions.prompt: Where will the shop keep the bag?
questions.explanation: The man states behind the counter, not outside or on a bus.

materials.title: Calling about a farm visit
materials.text:
Woman: Green Lane Farm. Good morning.
Ali: Hello. Our family would like to visit on Sunday. What time do you open?
Woman: At ten. The last entry is at three, and the farm closes at four.
Ali: Can we see the goats being fed?
Woman: Yes. That happens at eleven, near the red barn. Please watch with a staff member. Visitors must not give the animals their own food.
Ali: My sister is five. Does she need a ticket?
Woman: Yes. Children under four are free. A child ticket is four pounds, and an adult ticket is seven.
Ali: Can we bring lunch?
Woman: Yes. Use the picnic tables by the pond. The café also sells sandwiches.
Ali: What if it rains?
Woman: The farm still opens, but some paths may be muddy. Wear suitable shoes. If there is dangerous weather, we announce a closure on our booking page.
Ali: Thank you. We will check before leaving home.

questions.prompt: When is the last entry?
questions.explanation: Last entry is15:00;16:00 is closure and11:00 feeding.

questions.prompt: Where can visitors watch the goats being fed?
questions.explanation: Feeding is near the barn; café and tables are food areas for people.

questions.prompt: Does Ali’s five-year-old sister need a ticket?
options: No, everyone under six is free
questions.explanation: Only under-four children are free. A five-year-old needs the child ticket.

questions.prompt: Where may the family eat their own lunch?
questions.explanation: Own lunches are allowed at the picnic tables. Animal areas/path dining are not permitted locations stated.

questions.prompt: What should the family check before travelling?
options: The booking page for any closure
questions.explanation: Dangerous-weather closures appear on the booking page. Animal feeding from visitors is prohibited and ticket rules are already stated.

materials.title: The moon in the puddle
materials.text:
In this story, a young fox sees the moon reflected in a puddle. He thinks it has fallen from the sky. He runs to Owl's tree and calls for help.

Owl looks up. The real moon is still above the hill, but Fox is staring at the water. "Look carefully," says Owl. Before she can explain, Fox fetches a small bucket.

He lowers it into the puddle. The water shakes, and the bright circle breaks into many moving pieces. Fox is worried that he has broken the moon. He sits down so suddenly that his tail splashes into the water too.

Owl waits until the puddle is still. The circle comes back. She asks Fox to look up, then down. At last he sees the two bright shapes together.

"One moon, two views," he says slowly.

Fox puts the bucket away. On his walk home, he sees the moon in a window and again in the river. This time he does not call for help. He counts the places where its light appears, while the real moon travels above him.

questions.prompt: Why does Fox first call Owl?
options: He thinks the moon has fallen
questions.explanation: He mistakes the reflection for a fallen moon. The bucket comes later and his tail is present.

questions.prompt: What happens when the bucket enters the puddle?
options: The real moon falls from the hill
The reflection breaks into moving shapes
questions.explanation: Disturbed water changes the reflection; the moon/tree do not move that way.

questions.prompt: Why does Owl wait?
options: The water needs to become still
She wants Fox to buy a window
She is waiting for the sun to rise
questions.explanation: Still water restores a clear reflection. Sunrise/purchase are not part of the scene.

questions.prompt: What helps Fox understand?
questions.explanation: He compares real moon and reflection. The other actions do not occur.

questions.prompt: What does Fox do on the way home?
options: Carries the moon in his bucket
Asks everyone to rescue the moon
questions.explanation: He recognises window/river appearances without calling for help. No rescue or captured moon occurs.

materials.title: The little post bell
materials.text:
In this fictional village, Rabbit delivers letters along a narrow lane. Every house has a small box by the gate. Rabbit usually leaves a letter and rings a bell to tell the family it has arrived.

One morning, the bell at Hedgehog's gate makes no sound. Rabbit taps it twice, then leaves the letter safely in the box. He decides to mention the silent bell when he returns.

That afternoon, Hedgehog is waiting outside. "I wondered when you would come," she says. She has been expecting a letter from her sister. Rabbit points to the box, and Hedgehog finds the envelope inside.

"The letter was here all along," she says. "I listened for the bell instead of looking."

They inspect the bell together. A piece of dry leaf is caught inside. Hedgehog removes it, and the bell rings again. She thanks Rabbit for delivering the letter even when the signal failed.

The next day, Rabbit still rings the bell. Hedgehog enjoys its familiar sound, but she checks the box too. The bell is useful news about a delivery; it is not the letter itself.

questions.prompt: Where does Rabbit put letters?
questions.explanation: Each gate has a letterbox. Beds/bell interior are not delivery places.

questions.prompt: Why does Hedgehog wait outside?
options: She wants to stop all deliveries
She expects a letter from her sister
questions.explanation: Her sister’s expected letter is stated. Stopping post/lost bicycle are invented.

questions.prompt: What has happened to the letter that morning?
options: It is still at her sister’s house
It has been eaten by Rabbit
questions.explanation: Rabbit leaves it safely in the box despite the silent bell.

questions.prompt: What stops the bell from sounding?
options: A sleeping bird on the roof
questions.explanation: The leaf is removed and sound returns. The alternatives are not described.

questions.prompt: What does Hedgehog do afterwards?
options: Uses the bell and also checks the box
questions.explanation: She keeps the useful signal while checking the actual delivery. She does not destroy or refuse the system.

materials.title: Four family outings
materials.text:
The town visitor office offers four outings. The prices below are per person. Each outing must be booked before Friday noon.

| Outing | Time | Age | Price | Important information |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Canal Boat | Saturday 10:00–11:30 | All ages | £8 | Children under 12 must come with an adult. Life jackets supplied. |
| Hill Walk | Saturday 14:00–16:30 | 10 and over | £5 | Bring water and walking shoes. Uneven ground; no pushchairs. |
| Puppet Theatre | Sunday 11:00–12:00 | All ages | £6 | Indoors. Seats reserved at booking. No food during the show. |
| Garden Trail | Sunday 14:00–15:30 | All ages | £4 | Outdoor picture clues. One adult must accompany each family group. |

An adult needs a ticket as well as a child. Prices do not include travel to the starting point. Arrive fifteen minutes before the listed start. The office will contact booked visitors if an outing is cancelled. Boat and walking outings may change in unsuitable weather; the indoor show is unaffected by rain. Ask about access needs before paying, since the routes and venues differ.

questions.prompt: Which outing is suitable for a rainy-day indoor activity?
questions.explanation: Theatre is explicitly indoors; walk/trail are outdoor activities.

questions.prompt: When should Canal Boat visitors arrive?
questions.explanation: Arrival is15 minutes before10:00 Saturday, hence9:45.

questions.prompt: How much do one adult and one child pay for Garden Trail?
questions.explanation: Each pays£4, total£8. Four is one ticket, twelve not the two-person trail total.

questions.prompt: Which outing does not allow pushchairs?
questions.explanation: Hill Walk explicitly excludes pushchairs due to uneven ground. The other notices do not state that rule.

questions.prompt: What must happen before Friday noon?
options: Visitors must arrive at the starting point
questions.explanation: The deadline is for booking, not finishing or arrival on the weekend.

materials.title: Where to ask for help
materials.text:
During the school open day, four help desks provide different services. All are free to use. Students should stay with their visiting family unless a teacher has agreed otherwise.

| Desk | Place | Open | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Welcome | Main gate | 9:00–12:00 | Gives maps and the day’s programme. |
| Lost Property | Library entrance | 10:00–14:00 | Holds found bags, coats and small items. Describe an item before collecting it. |
| Club Information | Sports hall | 9:30–13:30 | Explains club activities and future joining dates. Does not collect payments. |
| Quiet Space | Room 6 | 9:00–14:30 | Offers a place to sit away from the busy halls. A staff member is present. |

The open day begins at 9:00 and ends at 14:30. Lunch is sold in the dining room from 11:30 to 13:00. It is separate from the free help-desk services. Visitors who find an item should take it to Lost Property after 10:00; before then, give it to a teacher at Welcome. For an urgent problem, ask the nearest member of staff instead of waiting for a particular desk to open.

questions.prompt: Where can a family get a programme at 9:15?
options: Club Information in the sports hall
questions.explanation: Welcome is open9:00. Lost Property opens10:00 and clubs9:30.

questions.prompt: What should someone do to collect a found coat?
options: Pay the club desk for it
questions.explanation: The collection rule requires description. No fee or closing-time delay is stated.

questions.prompt: Which desk is still open at 14:15?
questions.explanation: Quiet Space lasts14:30, Welcome12:00 and clubs13:30.

questions.prompt: Where should a bag found at 9:30 be taken?
options: Directly to the closed Lost Property desk
Home to keep until next week
questions.explanation: Before10:00, found items go to a teacher at Welcome. Keeping it or relying on the closed desk contradicts guidance.

questions.prompt: Which service is not included among the free desk services?
options: Buying lunch in the dining room
questions.explanation: Lunch is sold separately. Programmes and quiet seating are free help services.
